generation_notes: Revised to exactly 14 structurally conservative seeds grounded only in supplied sources and with unsupported issue claims removed. The library now prefers complete IEC 60870-5-104 APDUs where framing is explicitly documented: start byte 0x68, one-byte APDU length, four-byte APCI control field, and ASDU payload for I-format only. U-format TESTFR act/con frames are included because their exact control bytes are explicitly documented. ASDU layout follows the documented template order type_id, vsq, cause_of_transmission, common_address, information_object_address, with conservative fixed parameterization of 2-octet cause of transmission, 2-octet common address, and 3-octet information object address in little-endian form, matching the documented configurable field sizes and little-endian rules. C_SC_NA_1 seeds append the documented single_command_qualifier after the information_object_address. To avoid malformed repetition, no unsupported multi-object C_SC_NA_1 encoding is used; parser-depth coverage instead uses a valid VSQ sequence-format example on a generic ASDU envelope where the documented information object address is absent when isSequence is true. Diverse type identifiers from the supplied catalogs are used to broaden dispatcher coverage while keeping lengths self-consistent and frames mutation-friendly.

sequences.purpose: Provide a compact canonical IEC 60870-5-104 I-format APDU carrying a single command activation with one information object and a minimal execute-form qualifier.
sequences.expected_behavior: A 104-capable parser should accept the APDU framing, parse a one-object C_SC_NA_1 ASDU, and dispatch it as an activation-style single command with a minimal qualifier.
constraints_preserved: APDU start byte is 0x68 as documented
APDU length 0x0f matches the 15 bytes following the length byte
ASDU field order is type_id, vsq, cause_of_transmission, common_address, information_object_address

VSQ count is 1 with sequence flag clear
Cause of transmission uses value 6 activation with two octets present
Common address is two octets in little-endian form
Information object address is three octets in little-endian form
Single command qualifier is appended after the information object address for C_SC_NA_1

global_feedback: The library has good breadth across IEC 60870-5-104 framing styles and multiple TypeID/COT dispatcher values, and it avoids obvious copied crash material.

The main weakness is protocol correctness: many I-format APDUs have incorrect length bytes relative to the provided hex, and several seeds rely on undocumented or likely incomplete ASDU object payloads for the chosen TypeIDs.
The strongest seeds are the exact U-format TESTFR act/con frames because their control bytes are explicitly documented and self-contained.
Several command ASDUs are useful as mutation starting points because they preserve full framing and stable field order, but they should be fixed before inclusion in a high-quality initial corpus.
The candidate count exceeds the desired final selected seed count of 12, and at least two low-confidence seeds should be removed after length and payload corrections.
Stateful setup is only partially realized: the interrogation pair is directionally plausible for parser exercise, but the APCI control fields are all zeroed and do not model realistic 104 sequencing.
The plan-to-seed mapping drifts in places: some function-code coverage plans targeting specific causes are implemented with unrelated TypeIDs or different operations, reducing plan fidelity.
Conservative complete framing should be prioritized over semantic breadth; repairing APDU length consistency and choosing only well-supported ASDU bodies would materially improve the corpus.

Section: Message Templates
Template: ASDU
- Field: type_id
  Description: Protocol field 'type_id'. Layer: asdu. Role: type. Type: enum. Range: [1, 127]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: offset.
  Length: 8 bits
  Implementation constraints: must be one of the IEC 60870-5-101/104 valid TypeID values (1..127)
- Field: vsq
  Description: Protocol field 'vsq'. Layer: asdu. Role: control. Type: uint8. Constraints: 7-bit count 1..127, MSB=1 indicates sequence format, MSB=0 indicates non-sequence format. Range: [0, 127]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: mask.
  Length: 8 bits
  Implementation constraints: mask 0x7f applied to extract count, mask 0x80 applied to extract flag, bit-7 encodes format flag, bits 0-6 encode element count
- Field: cause_of_transmission
  Description: Protocol field 'cause_of_transmission'. Layer: asdu. Role: cause. Type: uint8|uint16. Constraints: parameters->sizeOfCOT determines 1 or 2 octets, bit-7 is P/N bit, bit-6 is T bit. Range: [0, 65535]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: offset|mask|length_check.
  Length: 8|16 bits
  Implementation constraints: sizeOfCOT in parameters object, sizeOfCOT set by standard configuration
- Field: common_address
  Description: Protocol field 'common_address'. Layer: asdu. Role: address. Type: uint8|uint16. Constraints: size determined by CS101_AppLayerParameters.sizeOfCA (1 or 2), little-endian byte order for 2-byte case. Range: [0, 65535]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: offset.
  Length: 8|16 bits
  Implementation constraints: must be placed immediately after COT field, sizeOfCA is fixed for a single link/connection
- Field: information_object_address

global_feedback: The library shows useful intent and covers several planned operations, but protocol correctness is uneven and too many seeds rely on speculative framing choices not fully supported by the supplied sources.
Standalone ASDU seeds are reasonable as parser-entry corpus material, but they are weaker than complete frames and may not be accepted by implementations expecting 101 or 104 transport framing.
The 104 APDU seeds are among the stronger entries because they include complete start-byte, length, control field, and ASDU payload structure, with internally consistent length fields.
The 101 variable-length frame seeds are weak because they omit checksum bytes and use a variable-length frame structure that is unlikely to be accepted as valid by real 101 parsers.

Several seeds use cause-of-transmission values in combinations that are structurally parseable but semantically odd for the chosen type_id; that can still help coverage, but it lowers confidence as initial valid seeds.

The deep-parser C_SC_NA_1 seed is likely malformed for VSQ count handling because the template only explicitly documents one information_object_address for C_SC_NA_1, and the encoded object repetition does not clearly follow a documented sequence-format rule.
The stateful C_IC_NA_1 sequence is directionally useful, but it is still only ASDU-shaped and lacks stronger evidence for a truly valid state setup across a concrete transport profile.
There is excessive redundancy among the cause-of-transmission coverage seeds; selecting 12 seeds should prioritize the better-framed 104 entries and only a small number of standalone ASDU variants.
Validator removal of unknown evidence ids does not itself invalidate seeds, but it is a sign that grounding is weaker than intended in several plans.
Issue enhancement is disabled, and the library appropriately avoids obvious crash-payload copying.

global_feedback: The library has good breadth across IEC 60870-5-104 framing styles and multiple TypeID/COT dispatcher values, and it avoids obvious copied crash material.

The main weakness is protocol correctness: many I-format APDUs have incorrect length bytes relative to the provided hex, and several seeds rely on undocumented or likely incomplete ASDU object payloads for the chosen TypeIDs.
The strongest seeds are the exact U-format TESTFR act/con frames because their control bytes are explicitly documented and self-contained.
Several command ASDUs are useful as mutation starting points because they preserve full framing and stable field order, but they should be fixed before inclusion in a high-quality initial corpus.
The candidate count exceeds the desired final selected seed count of 12, and at least two low-confidence seeds should be removed after length and payload corrections.
Stateful setup is only partially realized: the interrogation pair is directionally plausible for parser exercise, but the APCI control fields are all zeroed and do not model realistic 104 sequencing.
The plan-to-seed mapping drifts in places: some function-code coverage plans targeting specific causes are implemented with unrelated TypeIDs or different operations, reducing plan fidelity.
Conservative complete framing should be prioritized over semantic breadth; repairing APDU length consistency and choosing only well-supported ASDU bodies would materially improve the corpus.
